beats.text: Ask people where they stand, and almost everyone says: the middle.
Researchers asked over thirty thousand people in ten countries.
Five steps, from poorest to richest. Each dot is one person on their real step.
Now each dot jumps to where they thought they were.
In every country, at least two in three poorer people placed themselves too high.
And richer people placed themselves too low.
If you feel pretty average, so does almost everyone.

sources: Hoy & Mager (2021), Why Are Relatively Poor People Not More Supportive of Redistribution? Evidence from a Randomized Survey Experiment across Ten Countries, American Economic Journal: Economic Policy 13(4) – >30,000 people in Australia, India, Mexico, Morocco, Netherlands, Nigeria, South Africa, Spain, UK, US; among the poorest two quintiles, between 67.0 % (UK) and 94.4 % (Nigeria) overestimated their position; 37.1–63.1 % placed themselves in the middle quintile; only 5.0–29.1 % placed themselves correctly (working paper ECINEQ 2019-489, sec. 4.1).

Hvidberg, Kreiner & Stantcheva (2023), Social Positions and Fairness Views on Inequality, Review of Economic Studies 90(6), 3083–3118 – Danish survey (~9,400) linked to tax records: people ranked low think they rank higher, people in the upper part think they rank lower ('center bias'). Dots in the video: schematic (100 dots, 77 % of the poorer 40 % move up).
